subject: Listing tier map — regional availability & co-sell routing
body:
From: Amy Lee <amy.lee@enterprisecorp.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Marketplace packaging and regional coverage question

Hi Avery,

Thanks for the demo last week — EnterpriseCorp is close to an internal OK to pilot Redwood for a multi-region rollout. Before procurement starts, our cloud procurement and cloud partner teams need two things clarified for the contract:

1) Which packaging tiers will be listed per cloud (AWS vs Azure vs GCP)? We need a recommended map so our SREs know which SKUs to buy in each region.
2) Regional availability — are all SKUs available in us-east-1, us-west-2, and GCP-us-central? What about GovCloud and Azure Government (if we pursue a Fed instance later)?
3) Co-sell routing / lead registration — how do we register co-sell opportunities in each marketplace and who at Redwood will be the co-sell contact?

Would you be able to share a concise proposal we can attach to the procurement packet? We need something the sourcing team can sign off on by 11/24.

Thanks,
Amy
Amy Lee
Sr. Cloud Procurement Manager
EnterpriseCorp

---
From: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>
To: Amy Lee <amy.lee@enterprisecorp.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Marketplace packaging and regional coverage question

Hi Amy — great to hear you are close. I put together an initial tier-map and a short implementation plan; attaching a PDF with the proposed mapping and a compliance checklist. Quick summary below.

Attachment: redwood-listing-tier-map-v1.pdf (proposal + matrix)

Summary (short):
- Tiers: Core (entry), Scale (business), Enterprise (dedicated + SLOs).
- AWS: list Core and Scale across commercial regions (us-east-1, us-west-2). Enterprise will be a reserved offer in AWS Marketplace (private offer) with license/commit.
- Azure: list Core as transactable SaaS offer + Scale in Marketplace with co-sell registration. Enterprise will be available via Azure Reserved/Marketplace SaaS with an enterprise agreement addendum.
- GCP: list Core on GCP Marketplace as subscription; Scale as a private listing (partner-assisted) for co-sell. Enterprise handled off-marketplace (purchase order + reserved instances).

Notes on Gov/Fed: we can support GovCloud/Azure Government for Enterprise tier only — it requires additional compliance packaging and a separate on-prem or private deployment. See govcloud-compliance-matrix.xlsx.

Co-sell / lead routing suggestions:
- AWS: need a transactable listing + co-sell registration; Ben will be primary co-sell lead for AWS.
- Azure: camila will initiate co-sell registration and PRR submission.
- GCP: require partner registration + partner co-sell contact; we'll route through our GCP partner channel (Jonas).

Proposed next steps:
1) I’ll share the attached PDF with your procurement team.
2) Ben/Camila/Jonas will confirm required artifacts for each marketplace by 11/20.
3) If procurement signs off, we’ll produce a DocuSign for the Enterprise private offer.

Avery Johnson
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference
avery_johnson@redwood.com

---
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>, Amy Lee <amy.lee@enterprisecorp.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 08:44:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Marketplace packaging and regional coverage question

Amy — quick pricing / SKU notes from sales ops that will affect which SKUs we recommend per cloud:

- Core (entry): low-throughput hosted API; unit price applies per 1M tokens/month; available as transactable listing on AWS, Azure, GCP commercial regions. No reserved capacity.
- Scale (business): includes burst capacity, higher token limits, preferred routing; available as Marketplace transactable on Azure and GCP but for AWS we recommend using a listing + reserved capacity commit for predictable throughput. SKU names we propose:
  - RDW-Core (transactable)
  - RDW-Scale-Std (transactable/private depending on cloud)
  - RDW-Enterprise-Reserved (private offer)

Region gating: if EnterpriseCorp requires GovCloud/AzureGov, those SKUs will be RDW-Enterprise-Gov which are only offered as dedicated/private capacity. That requires a minimal 6-month commitment and additional compliance paperwork (outlined in the spreadsheet).

Lead routing / deal registration: we should register the opportunity in AWS Deal Registration and submit Azure PRR prior to co-sell kick-off. For AWS co-sell benefits (funding/marketing), they expect a transactable listing + registered deal. We can align the HubSpot deal to the Marketplace registration (I attached the quote PDF).

Ben Carter
Principal Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

---
From: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Amy Lee <amy.lee@enterprisecorp.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 10:21:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Marketplace packaging and regional coverage question

Amy — a couple operational caveats to call out (so procurement has clear expectations):

- Azure transactable SaaS: requires OAuth-based subscriber provisioning and a metering plan. We can support this, but it adds ~2 weeks of integration work and a test tenancy for Microsoft validation.
- AWS GovCloud: listing there is possible only for dedicated/isolated deployments; we need a separate account and attestation. That is why EnterpriseGov is private-only.
- GCP partner marketplace: partner-assisted listings require that we have a partner reseller flow enabled; timing depends on our partner ops queue.

I’ll take the PRR checklist for Azure and start the submission once we have the HubSpot deal and a lead contact. Jonas, can you confirm the partner enablement ETA for GCP?

Camila Reyes
Marketplace & Partner Ops, Redwood Inference

---

> Avery / Camila / Ben — ETA for partner enablement on GCP is ~10 business days from our partner team receiving signed MSA + partner form. I can fast-track if EnterpriseCorp is comfortable signing the DocuSign for the private offer.

Thanks everyone — this is very helpful.

Quick action items from EnterpriseCorp side:
- Procurement: they want the PDF and the HubSpot quote in the packet (I have those).
- Legal: they asked if Gov/AzureGov will require any contract addenda; you noted yes — please confirm a short list of the contract items we should expect.
- Co-sell: we want to register for AWS co-sell. Ben, can you complete the AWS Deal Registration this week?

If you can produce a single-page summary for procurement (one-pager they can staple to the purchase order) and send DocuSign for the Enterprise private offer, we’ll aim to complete signatures by 11/24.

Amy
